**Roseville Housing Authority (RHA) Project-Based Vouchers and Housing Choice Vouchers (jurisdiction includes Rocklin)**
- Agency: Roseville Housing Authority, a department of the City of Roseville (Housing Division, 916-774-5270, housing@roseville.ca.gov)
- Type: other
- Typical award: Rental subsidy, not capital. RHA (established October 2, 1974) administers tenant-based Housing Choice Vouchers for roughly 850 households (about 1,600 individuals) at or below 50% AMI in Roseville and Rocklin, plus VASH and Mainstream vouchers. It project-bases vouchers in new affordable developments (the City's news release on The Crawford, 265 units by USA Properties, cites eight RHA project-based vouchers) and runs a Project Based Voucher waiting list (waitlistcheck.com CA1217-4334). Payment standards effective October 1, 2026 and utility allowances effective June 1, 2026 are posted for Roseville (95661, 95678, 95747) and Rocklin.
- AMI requirement: HCV income limits: 50% AMI at admission (2026: 1 person $46,000, 4 persons $65,700), with 75% of new admissions at or below 30% AMI; PBV units must meet HUD HQS and the Housing Element directs RHA to expand use in high opportunity areas.
- Cycle: rolling (next: PBV commitments are requested from RHA during predevelopment; RHA reports quarterly to Council (next quarterly status update early 2027). Contact RHA before TCAC or CDLAC applications to secure a PBV commitment letter.)
- Layering notes: Roseville and Rocklin projects have two voucher sources: RHA (city) and Placer County Housing Authority (county record, PBVs and special-purpose vouchers); Rocklin is covered by both. PBVs raise achievable rents on 30% AMI units and support bond or 4% deals. Not a public works trigger by itself. Verified on the RHA page opened this pass.
- Source: https://www.roseville.ca.gov/departments/affordable_housing/housing_authority/index.php
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Roseville Housing Successor Low and Moderate Income Housing Asset Fund (SB 341 reports; Housing Element Program 12)**
- Agency: City of Roseville acting as Housing Successor to the former Redevelopment Agency; Housing Division
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Small gap loans and Homeless Prevention and Rapid Rehousing grants. Fund balance $2,379,350 at June 30, 2025 (FY2024-25 deposits $1,032,069, including $737,249 from the 20% share of City loan payoffs; FY2024-25 expenditures $434,196 with $0 for development). Past development loans: $5,760,000 to Mercy Housing for 623 Vernon Street (58 units, 2016 to 2018), $600,000 deferred loan to Junction Crossing (80 units, approved October 20, 2021), $500,000 to Hampstead's Prospera at Fiddyment workforce housing (104 units, approved April 3, 2024). HPRR spending is capped at $250,000 per year; on September 2, 2026 Council budgeted $1,250,000 from the fund for FY2026-27 together with $1,374,763 of PLHA.
- AMI requirement: Health and Safety Code 34176.1 targeting: development money must serve households at or below 80% AMI, with at least 30% spent on 30% AMI households and no more than 20% on 60% to 80% AMI; 55-year covenants used; no senior-only restriction issue (0% of assisted units senior-restricted in the last 10 years).
- Cycle: rolling (next: No NOFA; developers approach the Housing Division. Revenue is only loan repayments (projected through 2036), so expect commitments of a few hundred thousand dollars per project. The FY2025-26 SB 341 report is due by December 31, 2026.)

Stacks with LHTF and PIP money (record above), PLHA, county in-lieu fee loans and LIHTC. Excess surplus test: the balance must stay under the greater of $1,000,000 or four years of deposits, which pushes the City to commit funds. Read from the FY2024-25 SB 341 Report of Required Information posted on the Affordable Housing Funds page.

**Roseville Local Housing Trust Fund (LHTF) gap loans, including Prohousing Incentive Program (PIP) program income NOFA (Resolution 26-404, November 4, 2026)**
- Agency: City of Roseville Economic Development Department, Housing Division (316 Vernon Street, Suite 150; 916-774-5270; housing@roseville.ca.gov)
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Project-by-project gap loans from the City's Local Housing Trust Fund, which receives in-lieu fees, affordable purchase loan payoffs and state grant program income. Most recent round: a NOFA released August 31, 2026 offered $1,000,000 of PIP program income (from a $1,050,000 developer loan payoff on the City's 2023 PIP Round 1 award of $1,610,000) for predevelopment of lower-income rental housing; two applications were received (Eden Housing, 505 Royer, 58 senior units; Mercy Housing, Pleasant Grove Apartments Phase II, 49 units) and staff recommended reserving the full $1,000,000 for Pleasant Grove Phase II on November 4, 2026. Gap order: LIHTC and bonds first, then City LHTF or PIP reservation, then County or Housing Trust Placer money. **Roseville Residential Density Bonus (Zoning Ordinance Chapter 19.28) and Prohousing Designation renewal (Resolution 25-346, November 5, 2025)**
- Agency: City of Roseville Development Services Department, Planning Division (Lauren Hocker, Senior Planner, 916-774-5272)
- Type: density bonus
- Typical award: Regulatory incentive, not a subsidy. Chapter 19.28 mirrors Government Code 65915: bonuses of 20% to 50% for very low, lower and moderate income set-asides, 80% (or no limit near major transit) for 100% affordable projects, 20% for senior, foster youth, disabled veteran and homeless housing, 35% for student housing, land donation and child care bonuses, up to four incentives, parking caps (0.5 space per unit for qualifying projects near transit, none for 100% lower-income rental near transit or qualifying senior projects). Applications require a pro forma, an appraisal of the bonus value and a sources and uses statement showing the financing gap. Roseville was among the first ten Prohousing-designated jurisdictions (2022); the designation expired at the end of 2025 and Council authorized renewal on November 5, 2025 (application published for 30-day review through September 29, 2025). The City reports over $1 million in grants attributable to the designation and received $1,610,000 of PIP Round 1 funds in 2023.
- AMI requirement: State density bonus thresholds (5% very low, 10% lower, 10% moderate for-sale, or 100% affordable); Affordable Housing Agreement recorded for 55 years (rental) under Section 19.28.110.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Processed with entitlements; no deadline. HCD action on the Prohousing renewal application was pending at the time of the November 2025 hearing; confirm current designation status with Planning before claiming Prohousing points in MHP, AHSC or IIG applications.)
- Layering notes: No local enhancements beyond state law other than the explicit pro forma and appraisal submittal requirements. Density bonus units do not count toward the 10% specific plan goal, and the Regulatory Agreement can assign bonus units as part of the City's subsidy. Prohousing status gives bonus points on state NOFAs for projects located in Roseville (not available in Rocklin, Lincoln or Auburn, none of which held the designation as of this pass). Chapter text read on the zoneomics code mirror; Roseville's own code host (ecode360) returns partial PDFs only.

- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Roseville development impact fee deferral for affordable multifamily (Municipal Code Section 4.04.040, Ordinance 6830; Sierra Vista Apartments deferral, Resolution 26-336)**
- Agency: City of Roseville Economic Development Department (Gina McColl, 916-774-5452) with the Finance Department
- Type: fee waiver
- Typical award: Deferral, not waiver: city-controlled impact fees are deferred from building permit to final or certificate of occupancy, with interest at the City's pooled rate (ten-year average about 2.23%) and an administrative processing fee per permit. Deferrals of $100,000 or more need Council approval. Example approved September 16, 2026: about $2,987,339 deferred for the 192-unit Sierra Vista Apartments (Greek Orthodox Housing Corporation, parcel JM-30, 4950 Upland Drive), covering fire construction tax, sewer and water connection, drainage, SVSP traffic mitigation, citywide and neighborhood parks, bike trail, public benefit and solid waste fees (about $373,000 per building). For a 100% affordable project (three or more units, all units low, very low or extremely low income, Affordable Housing Agreement under Section 19.28.110, objective design standards, secured promissory note) payment may be pushed up to one year after the first certificate of occupancy. The City's policy is not to waive fees; CSCDA SCIP fee financing is also offered.
- AMI requirement: Standard deferral is open to any multifamily project on request; the extended one-year post-occupancy deferral requires 100% of units (except managers) affordable to low, very low or extremely low income households under a recorded Affordable Housing Agreement.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Request through the Economic Development Department when fee estimates are prepared; a Council hearing under Government Code 53083 is required for deferrals of $100,000 or more.)
- Layering notes: Timing relief only; fees are still paid in full with interest, so it does not reduce basis but eases construction-period cash needs. Placer County Capital Facilities fees and traffic fees are not city-controlled and are not deferred; age-restricted projects get reduced traffic and County capital facilities rates. Roseville also made a $571,850 CDBG loan (September 4, 2024) to the same Sierra Vista sponsor for land purchase, showing how CDBG, fee deferral, the Regulatory Agreement and LIHTC stack on one project. Read from the September 16, 2026 City Council agenda packet via the CivicClerk API file stream.
- Source: https://rosevilleca.api.civicclerk.com/v1/Meetings/GetMeetingFileStream(fileId=11713,plainText=false)
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)


### City of Sacramento

**City of Sacramento Development Impact Fee Deferral Program**
- Agency: City of Sacramento Community Development Department, Building Division (Form CDD-0330)
- Type: fee waiver
- Typical award: Deferral, not waiver: City impact fees may be paid at final inspection instead of permit issuance, useful for phased or multi-building projects. No cost figure published. Fee estimates available for a low-cost application. The Statewide Community Infrastructure Program (CSCDA SCIP) is also accepted for financing eligible City impact fees.
- AMI requirement: None; open to all residential projects.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Apply with CDD-0330 before permit issuance; fees due at final inspection.)
- Layering notes: Carries impact fees through construction so they can be paid from permanent loan proceeds; pair with the Zero-Dollar Rate reduction on the affordable units and SCIP bond financing of remaining fees. The County runs a separate deferral program for unincorporated projects (County record).
- Source: https://www.cityofsacramento.gov/community-development/planning/housing/housing-development-kit/housing-development-incentives/help-me-reduce-the-cost-of-development
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**City of Sacramento Housing Trust Fund (commercial linkage fee, City Code Chapter 18.56 Article IV)**
- Agency: City of Sacramento Community Development Department, Planning Division (fee assessment); SHRA (fund administration and lending)
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Fee source for SHRA City gap loans. Nonresidential rates effective July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2026: office $3.33, hotel $3.18, commercial $2.68, manufacturing $2.08, warehouse $0.91 per square foot, adjusted annually by the San Francisco construction cost index (the FY 2026-27 notice was not posted as of 2026-11-08). 2024 fund: $411,805 fees collected, $140,000 spent, $4.85M ending balance of which $807,861 uncommitted; $1.0M posted as available June 1, 2026.
- AMI requirement: Fund is restricted to housing for workforce households up to 80% AMI (very low and low income wage earners) under the 1989 jobs-housing nexus; 55-year SHRA regulatory agreement.
- Cycle: annual NOFA (next: Deployed through the SHRA two-round schedule (next pre-application likely early January 2027). Fee is paid at building permit on nonresidential projects; contact Ryan Dodge, (916) 808-8044, rdodge@cityofsacramento.org for fee questions.)
- Layering notes: Adopted 1989 (Chapter 17.708), moved into the Development Impact Fee chapter 18.56 on Feb 14, 2017; Council raised the fee 81.3% in 2004 (phased) and allows changes by resolution. Small and lumpy: about $0.4M to $0.6M a year in fees, so it is the smallest of the four City pools and is usually blended into a single SHRA loan with HOME and Mixed Income money. Parallel County Housing Trust Fund covers the unincorporated area (County rates $3.26 office to $1.08 warehouse since March 28, 2025). Annual report posted each May by SHRA.
- Source: https://www.cityofsacramento.gov/community-development/planning/housing/housing-trust-fund
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Density bonus (City Code Chapter 17.704) and ministerial infill housing permits (Chapter 17.860 and SB 35/SB 423)**
- Agency: City of Sacramento Community Development Department, Planning Division
- Type: density bonus
- Typical award: State density bonus law as implemented in Chapter 17.704 (no local enhancement beyond state minimums identified): e.g., 5% very low income units earns a 20% bonus plus one concession and unlimited waivers; up to 50% bonus and the 100% affordable 80% bonus per Government Code 65915. City ministerial permit (CDD-0428, adopted Aug 27, 2020) covers 2 to 200 unit residential or mixed-use infill projects meeting objective standards, no affordability or prevailing wage requirement, no CEQA, 60 to 90 day review; the state SB 35 permit (CDD-0427) requires 10% lower-income units at 11 or more units. Density bonus requests can be processed ministerially with either permit.
- AMI requirement: Per state law for the bonus; none for the City ministerial permit.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Rolling at entitlement. Parking: none required within a quarter mile of light rail, 50% reduction within a half mile.)
- Layering notes: Sacramento is the state's first Prohousing jurisdiction (renewed Dec 23, 2025 with the top score) and already has high base densities, so the bonus is mostly used for height, parking and setback waivers rather than unit count. Combining the City ministerial permit with a density bonus avoids hearings and CEQA for 100% affordable infill without the SB 35 prevailing wage trigger. Missing Middle zoning (2024) allows multi-unit on former single-family lots citywide.
- Source: https://www.cityofsacramento.gov/community-development/planning/housing/housing-development-kit/housing-development-incentives/help-me-build-more-housing-units-or-tailor-my-project-to-my-site
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Mixed Income Housing Ordinance and Housing Impact Fee (City Code Chapter 17.712)**
- Agency: City of Sacramento Community Development Department, Planning Division (fee); SHRA (Mixed Income Housing fund and 100-acre housing strategies)
- Type: other
- Typical award: Requirement and fee, not a subsidy. Housing Impact Fee effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027: $3.58 per square foot for single-unit, duplex and multi-unit dwellings below 20 and 40 dwelling units per net acre respectively; $0.00 for single-unit or duplex at 20 du/acre or more, multi-unit at 40 du/acre or more, and nonresidential-to-residential conversions; $1.55 per square foot in the Housing Incentive Zone. Fee revenue (about $1.7M in 2024, $4.2M lent to projects that year) goes to the SHRA-administered Mixed Income Housing fund; $2.5M posted available June 1, 2026. Projects over 100 gross acres must adopt a Council-approved mixed income housing strategy.
- AMI requirement: Exempt from the fee: developments with 10% regulated low-income units (80% AMI), room additions, second units, owner-builder single homes, mobilehome parks, projects with pre-ordinance development agreements or pre-November 2015 entitlements. No mandatory inclusionary requirement citywide.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Fee assessed at building permit, adjusted every July 1. The Housing Element Program H1 review ended Dec 9, 2025 when Council voted to make no changes, so the current structure holds through at least 2027. Contact Greta Soos, (916) 808-2027.)
- Layering notes: Most 4% and 9% multifamily deals in Sacramento pay nothing: at 40 du/acre or more the rate is $0, and any project with 10% low-income units is exempt, so the fee mainly hits single-family subdivisions and low-density apartments. The fund it feeds is the largest City gap pool after HOME ($2.5M June 2026). Compare the County Affordable Housing Ordinance ($3.91 per square foot with on-site credit) for unincorporated sites. A 2023 to 2025 study considered mandatory inclusionary and higher fees; Council declined, so no inclusionary units are required citywide.
- Source: https://www.cityofsacramento.gov/community-development/planning/housing/housing-impact-fee
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Multifamily Mortgage Revenue Bonds, Housing Authority of the City of Sacramento (SHRA conduit issuance)**
- Agency: Sacramento Housing and Redevelopment Agency for the Housing Authority of the City of Sacramento
- Type: bond
- Typical award: Tax-exempt and taxable conduit bonds for rental projects of 12 or more units in the City; no minimum or maximum issue size (cost-effectiveness usually sets a floor). Applications for bonds without an SHRA loan are accepted year round; bond-plus-loan requests follow the SHRA pre-application schedule. Private placements require accredited or qualified institutional buyers in $250,000 denominations with investor letters.
- AMI requirement: Federal minimum 20% at 50% AMI or 30% at 60% AMI plus 10% at 50% AMI (H&S 34312.3); CDLAC and CTCAC rules govern; SHRA adds its 15% at 50% AMI and 5% at 30% AMI policy when an SHRA loan is included; non-competitive CTCAC deals averaging above 60% AMI must average at or below 59% AMI. Refundings that extend maturity require at least 10% of units at 50% or 60% AMI for 15 more years.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Bond-only applications any time; bond-with-loan applications on the SHRA schedule (next pre-application likely early January 2027). SHRA Commission then City Council approval, then CDLAC allocation.)
- Layering notes: SHRA prefers to be the issuer for City projects and pairs bonds with its gap loan; CSCDA or CMFA remain alternatives if timing does not fit. Bond policy requires the nonprofit owner to have material day-to-day involvement for projects claiming the welfare exemption, matching BOE scrutiny of managing general partners (see County Assessor record). Policies: 2026 City Multifamily Lending and Mortgage Revenue Bond Policies (Section 9).
- Source: https://www.shra.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/2026-SHRA-Multifamily-Lending-Policies-City-final.pdf
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Prohousing Designation (state scoring preference for City of Sacramento projects)**
- Agency: City of Sacramento Community Development Department (designation held by the City; HCD administers the program)
- Type: other
- Typical award: Not a direct subsidy. Projects in a Prohousing jurisdiction receive priority processing or bonus points in state programs including AHSC, Infill Infrastructure Grant, TCC, TIRCP and related transportation programs, and the City may apply to the Prohousing Incentive Program for added funds. Sacramento was the first designated city (Feb 10, 2022) and renewed Dec 23, 2025 with 108 points, the highest score in the state as of June 2026.
- AMI requirement: None at the project level; benefit flows to any eligible affordable project in the City.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Designation runs on HCD's renewal cycle; next renewal due around 2029. Contact Angel Anguiano, (916) 808-5519.)
- Layering notes: Relevant to layering: AHSC and IIG applications for City sites score Prohousing points that unincorporated-county and most other Sacramento-area cities (Elk Grove, Rancho Cordova, Citrus Heights, Folsom were not confirmed as designated this pass) do not get. Check HCD's designated-jurisdictions tracker before assuming points for a non-City site.
- Source: https://www.cityofsacramento.gov/community-development/planning/housing/Prohousing
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Reduced Residential Development Impact Fees for Affordable Dwelling Units (Zero-Dollar Rate Program)**
- Agency: City of Sacramento Community Development Department, Planning Division (Form CDD-0410); affordability confirmed by SHRA or CADA
- Type: fee waiver
- Typical award: Reduction of City-controlled development impact fees to a $0 rate for deed-restricted affordable units, capped at $10,000 per qualifying unit, funded by a $3 million annual General Fund/Measure U appropriation (reauthorized July 2025). Eligible fees: park development impact fee (Ch. 18.56 Art. II), sewer, combined sewer, water system and storm drainage development fees (Ch. 13), and the 65th Street, Central City, Jacinto Creek, North Natomas, Railyards, River District and Willowcreek area fees. School fees and SAFCA fees are not City-controlled and still apply.
- AMI requirement: Rental: occupied by low or moderate income households (80% or 120% AMI per H&S 50093) at affordable rent (H&S 50053), restricted at least 30 years by a recorded regulatory agreement with the City, SHRA or another public agency. For-sale: low income (80% AMI) at an affordable price, 30 years.
- Cycle: rolling (next: First come, first served against each fiscal year's $3M; LIHTC and Homekey projects may reserve funds when awarded. Apply with Form CDD-0410 before permit issuance; contact planning@cityofsacramento.org early. Program resolutions 2018-0428, 2019-0185 and 2024-0233 (June 25, 2024).)
- Layering notes: Worth roughly $5,000 to $10,000 per unit depending on area fees; stackable with the SacSewer impact fee waiver (County record) which covers the regional sanitation fee the City program does not touch, and with the Housing Impact Fee $0 rate. Because Labor Code 1720(b)(4) treats waived fees as public funds, a fee reduction can by itself trigger state prevailing wage for a project that is otherwise exempt; most LIHTC projects already pay prevailing wage. The 2018 version waived fees without a cap; the 2024 modification added the $10,000 cap and the $3M budget, so large projects should not assume full waivers. Deferral of remaining impact fees to final inspection is available separately (CDD-0330).
- Source: https://www.cityofsacramento.gov/community-development/planning/housing/reduction-of-development-impact-fees-for-new-adus
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**SHRA Multifamily Lending Program (City of Sacramento gap financing: HOME, Housing Trust Fund, Mixed Income Housing fund, PLHA)**
- Agency: Sacramento Housing and Redevelopment Agency (SHRA) on behalf of the City of Sacramento and the Housing Authority of the City of Sacramento
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Gap loans sized to the gap after all other sources, no stated per-project cap. City funds posted June 1, 2026: HOME $5,000,000, Housing Trust Fund/Workforce Housing $1,000,000, Mixed Income Housing/Workforce Housing $2,500,000, PLHA $680,000 (about $9.2M). Applicants request gap funds without naming a source. January 2026 City pre-applications: Hotel Berry (Jamboree, preservation, $5.1M) invited; Florin Family Apartments (CCH, $5.1M) and Q Street Apartments (Community HousingWorks, $2.0M) invited; requests of $6.5M to $12M (Mercy 2601 5th Street, Danco 6779 Q Street, TWG 1220 H Street, Dos Rios) declined for insufficient funds. Projects must have 12 or more units.
- AMI requirement: 55-year regulatory agreement (HOME units per federal rules). SHRA minimum: at least 15% of units at or below 50% AMI and 5% at or below 30% AMI based on feasibility; regulated share at least proportional to SHRA share of total development cost; restricted rents at least 10% below market. Housing Trust Fund and Mixed Income fund money is limited to workforce households (up to 80% AMI, jobs-housing nexus). Priorities: preservation at risk, then new construction and nonresidential conversion (PSH and homeless housing, veterans, workforce 30% to 60% AMI, other), then rehab of regulated stock, then market-rate to affordable conversion.
- Cycle: annual NOFA (next: Two rounds a year aligned to CTCAC 9% rounds. 2026: pre-applications Jan 2 and July 1 (Builder's Patch), full applications March 2 and Sept 1, Council approvals June 16, 2026 and Jan 19, 2027. SHRA was not accepting pre-applications as of 2026-11-08; the 2027 schedule and a new funds-available notice are expected on the SHRA multifamily page at least 30 days before the next pre-application deadline, likely early January 2027. Phone (916) 440-1393.)
- Layering notes: This is the City-side pool parallel to the County SHRA record (Pass 2); a project uses one or the other based on location, both run on the same schedule and policies (2026 City Multifamily Lending and Mortgage Revenue Bond Policies, amended July 29, 2026). Terms: up to 3% simple interest or the AFR, term up to 40 years from conversion or 55 years when senior public lenders require, 1.10x to 1.20x combined DSCR, payments deferred during construction and deferred developer fee repayment, residual receipts allowed; nonprofit managing general partner required; developer fee limited to $25,000/$15,000/$12,000 per unit tiers for non-tax-credit deals and deferred maximum fee for LIHTC deals. Federal HOME (12 or more units) and CDBG (8 or more units) trigger Davis-Bacon; SHRA treats state prevailing wage as applying unless the below-market loan exemption (40% of units at 80% AMI for 20 years) fits. Stack with the City Zero-Dollar Rate impact fee reduction, Housing Impact Fee exemption at 40 du/acre, SacSewer fee waivers (County record) and Housing Authority of the City of Sacramento bonds. SHRA does not expect a project-based voucher RFP in 2026. SB 802 moves SHRA into the Sacramento Area Housing and Homelessness Agency by Jan 1, 2028, so confirm the lender entity on 2027 and later commitments.
- Source: https://www.shra.org/multi-family-housing-financing-lending-resources/
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)


### City of San Carlos

**Below Market Rate (BMR) Ordinance (SCMC Chapter 18.16, revised June 2022)**
- Agency: City of San Carlos Community Development Department, Planning and Housing
- Type: other
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. 15% of units in market-rate developments: rental 10% very low plus 5% low income (or an option of 15% very low income to align with state density bonus law); ownership 10% moderate plus 5% low income, raised to 20% low income by the June 2022 revisions. On-site units required at 7 or more rental units and 5 or more ownership units; smaller projects pay an in-lieu fee.
- AMI requirement: Deed restrictions with City BMR eligibility rules (SCMC 18.16.080), San Carlos resident and worker preference, County income limits (2026 AMI $200,800 for four).
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at entitlement; in-lieu fee amount in the Master Fee Schedule (not opened).)
- Layering notes: County layer: every San Mateo County city project competes for the County Affordable Housing Fund NOFA (AHF 14 closed July 15, 2026, next fall 2027), HEART bridge loans and HACSM project-based vouchers; city money is usually the first commitment that unlocks those. The very low income rental tier makes San Carlos BMR units eligible to pair with HACSM PBVs; recent downtown projects at 1232 to 1360 Cherry Street used the ordinance's density bonus alignment. Source is the Housing Resources chapter of the 2023-2031 Housing Element.
- Source: https://cms3.revize.com/revize/sancarlos/Document%20Center/Housing%20Element/05%20San%20Carlos%20Housing%20Resources_Final.pdf
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-07)

**Commercial Linkage Fee fund loans and City land for affordable housing (Cherry Street Commons)**
- Agency: City of San Carlos Community Development Department, Housing Division (housing successor to the former Redevelopment Agency)
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Commercial Linkage Fee (SCMC Chapter 8.51, adopted 2016) on large office and life science projects had produced over $10 million by 2023 with more than $30 million projected over the following five years. Council approved a $12,860,000 construction loan on June 26, 2023 for Cherry Street Commons (Eden Housing and HIP Housing, 33 family units, one to three bedrooms, replacing a six-unit HIP building at 1244 Cherry Street on City land including 1232 Cherry Street acquired in 2022, occupancy targeted 2026) and forgave a $100,000 1995 loan on 1244 Cherry in FY 2024-25. Housing successor assets total about $9 million (817 Walnut Street ground lease and $10.4 million of loans receivable) with a slight cash deficit. A NOFA 25-26 is listed on the City housing page without details.
- AMI requirement: Lower income households under City regulatory agreements; housing successor funds limited to 80% AMI with extremely low income minimums.
- Cycle: rolling (next: No open solicitation found; the City lists a NOFA 25-26 but the link resolves to the homepage. Contact the Housing Division at (650) 802-4265.)
- Layering notes: County layer: every San Mateo County city project competes for the County Affordable Housing Fund NOFA (AHF 14 closed July 15, 2026, next fall 2027), HEART bridge loans and HACSM project-based vouchers; city money is usually the first commitment that unlocks those. San Carlos is cash-rich from life science linkage fees and land-rich downtown (Walnut Studios at 817 Walnut was the first City-financed project), so it funds projects at a much higher per-unit level than its neighbors; the per-square-foot linkage rate is in the Master Fee Schedule and was not confirmed this pass (codepublishing.com returned 403). Source is the City's Cherry Street Commons page; loan amount from the June 27, 2023 announcement (vmwp.com) and the FY 2024-25 Housing Successor Annual Report.
- Source: https://www.cityofsancarlos.org/city_hall/departments_and_divisions/community_development/housing/cherry_street_commons.php
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-07)


### City of San Leandro

**HOME Investment Partnerships Program through the Alameda County HOME Consortium (Cooperative Agreement FY 2027-2029, Council item 26-152) and PLHA**
- Agency: City of San Leandro Community Development Department, Housing Services Division, 835 East 14th Street; housing@sanleandro.org, (510) 577-6006
- Type: grant
- Typical award: San Leandro is too small for a direct HUD HOME allocation and has been a Consortium member since 1992. FY 2027 HOME allocation $201,134 ($190,548 program, $10,586 admin); prior-year balances $593,119; combined $783,667 committed March 2026 to Eden Housing for rehabilitation of The Surf (46 affordable units). Past HOME projects: Estabrook Place (51 senior units), Marea Alta (115 family units). PLHA formula funds support a BACS homelessness prevention shallow subsidy program (18 months, FY 2025-26 to 2026-27) and are offered for development through the City RFP.
- AMI requirement: HOME: 80% AMI and HOME rents; PLHA: per state PLHA plan, Housing First for services.
- Cycle: annual NOFA (HOME program year; projects selected through the City's Multifamily Affordable Housing Rehabilitation and Preservation selection process) (next: FY 2028 allocation expected spring 2027; HOME FY 2024 funds must be expended by June 30, 2027. The County may centralize HOME awards under the FY 2027-2029 agreement.)
- Layering notes: Duplicates the county HOME Consortium record in mechanism but the City controls its own formula share and selects the project. Recent use is rehabilitation of existing affordable stock rather than new construction. Pairs with the County HOME RFP, Measure A1 and 4% credit recapitalizations.
- Source: https://legistar1.granicus.com/SanLeandro/attachments/ee1d0cbf-da8d-402e-bc23-86d2e977062a.pdf
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Inclusionary Housing Ordinance, San Leandro Zoning Code Chapter 6.04 (Ordinance 2004-023, amended 2020-002), in-lieu fee and Affordable Housing Trust Fund (6.04.156)**
- Agency: City of San Leandro Community Development Department, Housing Services Division, 835 East 14th Street; housing@sanleandro.org, (510) 577-6006
- Type: other
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. At least 15% of units in residential developments must be inclusionary units for moderate, low or very low income households (density bonus units excluded from the base); for-sale projects of 2 to 6 units may pay an in-lieu fee equal to (median San Leandro sales price minus affordable ownership cost) times a fractional unit of 0.30 to 0.90; larger projects may combine fees with off-site alternatives only with approval. Exempt: for-sale projects and condo conversions under 2 units and rental projects under 4 units. Fees, condo conversion fees and loan repayments go to the Affordable Housing Trust Fund. FY 2025 AHTF revenue $24,682 (no in-lieu fees), balance $336,166 at June 30, 2025 (FY 2024 restated to $311,484 after audit). Recent BMR production: Centro Callan (10 BMR rental units), Poppy Lane (3 BMR homes).
- AMI requirement: 15% of units for moderate, low or very low income households; rental inclusionary units subject to recorded covenants administered under the BMR Procedural Manual (SLMC 19.172.030).
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at map or planning approval; the 2023-2031 Housing Element commits to an economic feasibility study and ordinance amendments during the cycle (not yet scheduled).)
- Layering notes: The AHTF is too small to fund projects on its own; it has covered predevelopment grants and a site acquisition contribution. The ordinance predates AB 1505 and still exempts small rental projects; developers of rental projects with 4 or more units owe 15% on-site, which is above Hayward's and Fremont's rental percentages and a cost consideration for mixed-income deals. Ordinance text read on the zoneomics mirror (qcode is blocked); fund figures from the FY 2025 AHTF report adopted by Resolution 2025-163 (December 15, 2025).
- Source: https://www.sanleandro.org/DocumentCenter/View/10247
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Park Facilities Development Impact Fee exemption and 50% reduction for affordable units (Administrative Code Section 8.8.121, Council item 25-347, July 2025)**
- Agency: City of San Leandro Community Development Department and Recreation and Parks
- Type: fee waiver
- Typical award: Park impact fees restructured in July 2025 from per-unit-type ($18,074 per multifamily unit in FY 2024-25) to unit-size tiers: under 550 sq ft $6,052; 550 to 750 sq ft $7,565; 751 to 1,150 sq ft $11,600; 1,151 to 1,650 sq ft $16,140; 1,651 to 1,950 sq ft $20,679; over 1,950 sq ft $25,723 (land acquisition plus improvement components, CPI and ENR indexed). New Section 8.8.121: a residential development is exempt from the park fee if 100% of units (excluding manager units) are affordable and the applicant is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit or controlled by one; any other affordable unit pays 50% of the otherwise applicable rate. ADU fees eliminated by companion resolution.
- AMI requirement: Affordable unit per Health and Safety Code 50093 with affordable rent (50053) or affordable housing cost (50052.5) under a recorded restrictive covenant; full exemption requires 100% affordable nonprofit ownership.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at building permit; fees index annually. Confirm adoption of the final ordinance and resolution (introduced July 1, 2025) with the City Clerk.)
- Layering notes: The only development fee relief among the five priority cities that is written into local code for 100% affordable nonprofit projects (Oakland's AHIF exemption is comparable in effect). Saves roughly $6,000 to $12,000 per small unit. Other City fees (building permit, sewer connection) are not waived; school and EBMUD fees are outside City control. The document read was the draft resolution attached to the July 1, 2025 Council item on Legistar.
- Source: https://legistar1.granicus.com/SanLeandro/attachments/dbe7f4a0-f45c-4e92-aa84-0a1966b90411.pdf
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Residential Density Bonus, San Leandro Zoning Code Chapter 6.08, and inclusionary incentives (6.04.136)**
- Agency: City of San Leandro Community Development Department, Planning Division
- Type: density bonus
- Typical award: Requirement and entitlement, not a subsidy. Chapter 6.08 grants the bonus, incentives and concessions exactly as specified in Government Code 65915, processed concurrently with other entitlements and approved if the applicant complies with state law; continued availability of bonus units secured by agreement. Section 6.04.136 allows additional flexibility in density, lot size, yards and parking to accommodate required inclusionary units, but density bonus affordable units are in addition to the inclusionary requirement. Condominium conversions get the 65915.5 bonus (5.32.136).
- AMI requirement: State thresholds; inclusionary 15% must still be met on the base project.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Concurrent with the entitlement application.)
- Layering notes: No local enhancement beyond state law. San Leandro's affordable housing tools beyond density bonus are the inclusionary ordinance, the small AHTF, the HOME/PIP/PLHA RFP and the 2025 park fee exemption; there is no fee waiver for building permits and no local trust fund NOFA with meaningful capital. Code read on the zoneomics mirror.
- Source: https://www.zoneomics.com/code/san-leandro-CA/chapter_6
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**San Leandro Affordable Housing Development RFP (released February 28, 2025, continuous): HOME, Prohousing Incentive Program and PLHA funds**
- Agency: City of San Leandro Community Development Department, Housing Services Division, 835 East 14th Street; housing@sanleandro.org, (510) 577-6006
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Open-ended RFP for affordable housing development loans from the City's HOME Consortium share, Prohousing Incentive Program award and PLHA allocation; amounts available on request to the Housing Division. HOME available as of April 2026: $201,134 FY 2027 ($190,548 program) plus $593,119 prior-year funds (FY 2024 $225,238 due 6/30/2027, FY 2025 $179,013, FY 2026 $188,868); $783,667 committed to Eden Housing for rehabilitation of The Surf (46 units, 15320 Tropic Court). PLHA also funds a BACS shallow rental subsidy program. City contributions to the Lewelling interim housing project (HCEB, opened 2025) were $65,000 predevelopment and $309,500 acquisition from the AHTF.
- AMI requirement: Regulatory agreement typically 55 years; PLHA-funded projects must follow Housing First; HOME units at or below 80% AMI; priority to people experiencing or at risk of homelessness.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Continuous until funds are committed; HOME FY 2024 funds must be spent by June 30, 2027. Contact Housing Services before applying.)
- Layering notes: San Leandro's local money is thin (AHTF balance $336,166 at June 30, 2025), so the RFP mainly packages federal and state pass-throughs. Realistic stack: County Measure A1 San Leandro base allocation and regional pool, Measure W, HACA project-based vouchers, AHSC (City co-applied with Pacific West Communities in Rounds 9 and 10 for a BART-area project), and CMFA or County conduit bonds. The City expects the County to centralize HOME administration for FY 2027-2029. RFP read on the City's DocumentCenter; some sanleandro.org pages returned 403 after repeated requests.
- Source: https://www.sanleandro.org/DocumentCenter/View/12099
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)


### City of San Mateo

**Affordable Housing Commercial Linkage Fee fund (SMMC Chapter 23.61)**
- Agency: City of San Mateo Community Development Department
- Type: other
- Typical award: Fee on net new nonresidential construction over 5,000 square feet, adopted September 2016 (Ordinance 2016-8): office, R&D and medical office $32.76 per square foot, hotel $13.11, retail, restaurant and services $6.55 (FY 2025-26 and FY 2026-27). 25% rebate for projects that sign a Standard Wage (area standard or prevailing wage) agreement; alternative of building 8 low-income units per 100,000 square feet of office, 3 per 100,000 of hotel, 1 per 100,000 of retail. Fund activity FY 2025-26: beginning $3,551,934, fees $1,090,711, loan repayments $514,717, ending balance $5,292,314 with $1,000,000 set aside for the Bespoke project and $4,000,000 programmed for housing land purchase.
- AMI requirement: Fund must support creation or preservation of housing for lower and moderate income workers; projects carry City regulatory agreements.
- Cycle: rolling (next: No NOFA. The City commits linkage fee money by Council action; the FY 2025-26 report programs $4 million toward housing land purchase. Contact housing@cityofsanmateo.org, (650) 522-7220.)
- Layering notes: County layer: every San Mateo County city project competes for the County Affordable Housing Fund NOFA (AHF 14 closed July 15, 2026, next fall 2027), HEART bridge loans and HACSM project-based vouchers; city money is usually the first commitment that unlocks those. With about $4.3 million unprogrammed, the City can make one meaningful land or gap commitment per cycle rather than run a competitive round; developers should pair a request with the County AHF spring NOFA. The City is a CDBG entitlement (FY 2026-27 CDBG NOFA ran through the City) and joins the County HOME Consortium. Source is the FY 2025-26 Mitigation Fee Act (AB 1600) annual report; fee rates confirmed in the FY 2026-27 Comprehensive Fee Schedule and the Development Fees handout (DocumentCenter/View/98263).

**Below Market Rate (BMR) inclusionary program and in-lieu fees (SMMC 27.16.050)**
- Agency: City of San Mateo Community Development Department, Neighborhood Improvement and Housing Division
- Type: other
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. Projects of 11 or more units: 15% of rental units for lower income households (rents at 30% of 50% to 70% AMI, 4% annual increase cap) and 15% of ownership units for moderate income (100% to 110% AMI). Projects of 5 to 10 units and fractional units pay the BMR Housing Fee (Resolution 121 of 2008; FY 2026-27 schedule: rental $171,273 for a 5-unit project up to $342,545 for 10 units, ownership $157,187 to $314,373; fractional units $34,255 per 0.1 rental unit and $31,438 per 0.1 ownership unit). In-lieu fees are otherwise not allowed. BMR Housing Fee fund balance $254,281 at June 30, 2026 with $2,560,924 programmed for housing land purchase.
- AMI requirement: 55-year restrictions; BMR units may be up to 10% smaller than market units (20% where market units exceed 2,000 square feet); density bonus projects must provide BMR units equal to at least 15% of the base density; off-site and applicant-proposed alternatives need Council findings (Guidelines Resolution 72, June 16, 2025).
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at planning application; fees indexed in the annual Comprehensive Fee Schedule each July 1. The City is a participant in the 2026 multi-city nexus study.)
- Layering notes: County layer: every San Mateo County city project competes for the County Affordable Housing Fund NOFA (AHF 14 closed July 15, 2026, next fall 2027), HEART bridge loans and HACSM project-based vouchers; city money is usually the first commitment that unlocks those. San Mateo's program is unit-first: no fee option above 10 units, so inclusionary units are a given in every downtown and Hillsdale project and the City's cash sources are the Commercial Linkage Fee and the small BMR fee. Source is the adopted FY 2026-27 Comprehensive Fee Schedule (pages 11.1 to 11.2); program rules from the BMR Guidelines (cityofsanmateo.org/DocumentCenter/View/99291) and the FY 2025-26 Mitigation Fee Act report (DocumentCenter/View/107918).

### City of San Rafael

**Affordable Housing Requirement (inclusionary), SRMC 14.16.030(B), Ordinance 1990 and Resolution 14890 guidelines, in-lieu fee set by Resolution 15179**
- Agency: City of San Rafael Community and Economic Development Department, Planning and Housing Divisions
- Type: other
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. In-lieu fee per required affordable unit: $396,702 for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 ($389,032 in FY 2025-26, $368,274 in FY 2024-25, $362,817 in FY 2023-24), indexed annually to the California Construction Cost Index under Resolution 15179 (Dec 19, 2022). Fees are paid before building permit issuance and deposited to the Affordable Housing Trust Fund.
- AMI requirement: Primary requirement: projects of 2 to 15 units provide 10% of base units (excluding density bonus units) for low income households; projects of 15 or more units provide 5% low income. Secondary requirement for projects over 15 units: an additional 5% low income or 10% moderate income on site, or an in-lieu fee equal to 5% of base units, or off-site units within a half mile with an experienced affordable developer, or land donation appraised at or above the fee. Affordability in perpetuity, reducible to not less than 40 years on a Council finding of financial infeasibility. Fractional units below 0.5 pay the fee; 0.5 and above round up. Exempt: single-family homes, ADUs and JADUs, projects with pre-ordinance development agreements.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Fee resets every July 1; FY 2027-28 figure will post after the index update. Resolution 14890 requires a program review every 3 to 5 years, so watch for amendments alongside the 2027 Housing Element mid-cycle work.)
- Layering notes: Low on-site percentages (5% to 10%) make San Rafael one of the lighter inclusionary regimes in Marin, compared with Novato's 20% and Mill Valley's 15% (25% before 2026) and the County's 20%. Developers of 100% affordable projects satisfy the requirement automatically and the City counts inclusionary units with density bonus units when they overlap, which is why in-lieu receipts have dropped (Oct 2026 staff report). The Northgate Town Square redevelopment (Merlone Geier, up to 1,422 units, entitled Dec 2, 2024, demolition began fall 2025) is the largest pipeline source of inclusionary units or fee revenue; the City pages opened state that it includes affordable housing but do not quantify the count, so confirm the development agreement terms in the Laserfiche project documents before relying on them. Fee revenue funds the Trust Fund record above. Ordinance 1990, Resolutions 14890 and 14891 were opened as PDFs on the City fees page; Resolution 15179 is on the City's Laserfiche public records portal, which refused connections this pass.

**San Rafael Affordable Housing Trust Fund (Affordable Housing In-Lieu Fee Fund 243), Resolution 14760 guidelines, periodic NOFA and rolling acquisition process**
- Agency: City of San Rafael Community and Economic Development Department, Housing Division (Alexis Captanian, Housing Manager, (415) 485-3383, housing@sanrafael.gov)
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Small gap fund capitalized by residential in-lieu fees and commercial linkage fees. Balance was $2,034,226 in July 2023 and about $1,000,000 unencumbered on August 15, 2024. 2023 NOFA offered $1,400,000 and awarded $1,450,000 across three projects (BRIDGE Housing rehabilitation of 125 units at Nova Albion and Las Gallinas $1,000,000; Eden Housing 3301 Kerner Blvd 40-unit PSH adaptive reuse $250,000 on top of $2,101,663 prior awards; Canal Alliance Marin Villa Estates renovation $200,000). The June 2025 round awarded $600,000 across three projects (an acquisition, a rehabilitation and new construction) and was issued jointly with Marin County. Rolling acquisition process approved September 3, 2024: up to $250,000 per year total, unawarded amounts do not roll over. Awards are grants or loans at Council discretion.

Typical use is last-mile gap money of $200,000 to $1,000,000 that unlocks the Marin County Affordable Housing Fund (County guidelines require a city contribution for projects inside city limits) and County PLHA (2023 example: $250,000 City plus $250,000 County Trust Fund plus $250,000 PLHA for 3301 Kerner). - Agency: City of San Rafael Community and Economic Development Department, Planning Division
- Type: density bonus
- Typical award: Requirement framework, not a cash subsidy. Resolution 14891 (Feb 16, 2021) implements Government Code 65915 by Council resolution so tables update without a code amendment: Table 3 scales bonuses from 20% at 5% very low or 10% lower income up to 50% at 15% very low or 24% lower income, 35% at 40% moderate ownership, 20% for senior housing, land donation, supportive housing and student housing categories, and 80% or unlimited density with a three-story height increase for 100% affordable projects within a half mile of a major transit stop. ### City of San Ramon

**San Ramon Affordable Housing Commercial Linkage Fee (Inclusionary Housing and Commercial Linkage Ordinance, April 2019) and Affordable Housing Fund**
- Agency: City of San Ramon Community Development Department, Planning Services Division
- Type: other
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. A per square foot fee on net new gross floor area of all new commercial construction, including the commercial portion of mixed-use projects, regardless of zoning; exempt: projects adding 5,000 square feet or less, schools and places of public assembly, public facilities, and like-for-like replacement of buildings destroyed by calamity. Developers may instead build affordable units on an appropriate site, dedicate land or provide other housing resources. Mixed-use developments that meet the inclusionary policy are exempt from in-lieu fees. Fees are deposited into the City's Affordable Housing Fund ($4.28 million as of March 3, 2022, before Canopy and other recent payments). The per square foot rate is set in the Master Fee Schedule and was not found on an opened page.
- AMI requirement: Not applicable to the payer; the fund supports very low (including extremely low), low and moderate income rental and ownership housing in San Ramon.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at building permit. Housing Element Program 8 called for a 2024 review of the linkage fee structure to reflect affordable construction costs; the Council considered updated nexus fee studies with the FY 2026-27 Master Fee Schedule in March 2026 (confirm adopted rate).)
- Layering notes: Bishop Ranch and the City Center office base make this the City's steady fund source; the Affordable Housing Fund has no published NOFA and is deployed by Council through development agreements and project-specific commitments (the City adopted Priority Access System guidelines for City-funded projects), so developers should request Affordable Housing Fund support directly in entitlement negotiations. Stack with County HOME and Measure X (San Ramon is in the Urban County for HOME and CDBG, county records), HACCC project-based vouchers and the City's fee waiver policy (separate record). **San Ramon Affordable Rental Housing Fee Waiver Policy (adopted October 11, 2022) for 100% affordable rental projects**
- Agency: City of San Ramon Community Development Department, Planning and Building Divisions
- Type: fee waiver
- Typical award: Waiver of development impact fees and a capped waiver of City service fees for rental projects in which all units are affordable to households at or below 80% AMI. Impact fee waiver options: City Traffic Impact Fee, School Age Child Care Fee, Park and Recreation Facility Impact Fee, Private Sector Art and Beautification Fee, Open Space Development Impact Fee, Specific Plan Recovery Fees, General Plan Recovery Fee, Zoning Ordinance Recovery Fee and the Tri-Valley Transportation Development Fee (already waived for affordable units). City service fee waivers (building plan check and inspection, planning plan check, engineering plan check and inspection) capped at 25%. City example: a typical 100-unit affordable project receives about $24,000 per unit in impact fee waivers and $5,865 per unit in service fee waivers, over $2.5 million total. The City counts waived fees as local match for State funding applications; value calculated at building permit.
- AMI requirement: 100% of units (except managers' units) affordable to households at or below 80% AMI under a recorded affordable housing or density bonus agreement; San Ramon's 2026 rent table caps 80% AMI rents at $2,376 (1 person) to $3,938 (6 persons).
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at building permit issuance; no application deadline. The Canopy (BR 8) Eden Housing project (161 units, 2026 entitlements) and Eden's 2453 Camino Ramon project are the first users; confirm the policy remains in the FY 2026-27 Master Fee Schedule.)
- Layering notes: The only formal fee waiver program among the five priority cities and worth roughly $3 million on a 100-unit deal; combined with Bishop Ranch land dedications it makes San Ramon unusually feasible for 100% affordable 4% credit deals despite high land costs. Waivers are public funds for Labor Code 1720 purposes (prevailing wage) and are reported as local match to TCAC and HCD. Layer with County HOME and Measure X, HACCC PBVs and County conduit bonds (county records); the County has no comparable fee waiver program (county record: development fee waiver for affordable housing, discretionary only). Policy terms read from the HCD-hosted Housing Element (source_url) and confirmed in the January 13, 2026 Canopy staff report on the City's IQM2 host.

**San Ramon Density Bonus Ordinance (Zoning Ordinance Division D4, Chapter VIII, Sections D4-76 to D4-80) and Priority Access System for City-funded housing**
- Agency: City of San Ramon Community Development Department, Planning Services Division
- Type: density bonus
- Typical award: Regulatory incentive, not a cash subsidy. Chapter VIII implements Government Code 65915 by reference: any changes to state density bonus law supersede local text; waivers of development standards are granted unless specified findings are made; parking may be modified or covered-parking requirements waived for affordable units; a density bonus housing agreement is recorded before final map or building permit; a processing fee set by resolution applies. No local bonus beyond state law. Separately, the City's Priority Access Guidelines give San Ramon residents and workers priority in City-funded affordable projects, and the Housing Element targets 200 very low or extremely low, 200 low and 400 moderate income inclusionary units over 2023-2031 against a RHNA of 5,111 units.
- AMI requirement: State density bonus law thresholds (Gov. Code 65915); density bonus units are excluded from the inclusionary unit count under C4-177, so they stack on top of the 15% inclusionary requirement.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at entitlement; no deadline.)
- Layering notes: San Ramon has no city-run NOFA, no RDA successor housing fund (the City never had a redevelopment agency) and its Affordable Housing Fund is deployed by Council through development agreements rather than competitive rounds; local tools are the inclusionary receiver-site model, the fee waiver policy and state density bonus. Most existing affordable stock in Dougherty Valley sits under Contra Costa County affordability agreements (county records: Inclusionary Housing Ordinance Ch. 822-4 and Residential Density Bonus Ch. 822-2) rather than City agreements. Zoning text read on the zoneomics mirror (source_url); the City's code host (qcode) is blocked.

**San Ramon Inclusionary Housing Ordinance (Ordinance 520, adopted October 24, 2023; San Ramon Municipal Code Sections C4-175 to C4-183) and Affordable Housing Fund (C4-180)**
- Agency: City of San Ramon Community Development Department, Planning Services Division (Lauren Barr, Director; Planning@sanramon.ca.gov, 925-973-2560)
- Type: other
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. Applies to all residential projects of 2 or more units (ADUs excluded). Projects of 2 to 9 units (for-sale or rental) may pay an affordable housing fee equal to 25% of total new livable square footage times the per square foot rate in the City Fee Resolution (about $15.16 per square foot per the City of Antioch's January 2026 countywide comparison). For-sale projects of 10 or more units (single-family and multifamily) must build 15% affordable units allocated 20% very low, 30% low and 50% moderate income (must-build added in 2023). Rental projects of 10 or more units must provide 15% affordable units, half very low and half low income. Alternatives (C4-179): voluntary rental units in a for-sale project, off-site construction within San Ramon, preservation of at-risk units with 55-year extensions, land dedication (fully improved with impact fees paid) or combinations. Fees go to the Affordable Housing Fund with an annual report to Council on balance and commitments; the balance was $4.28 million as of March 3, 2022.
- AMI requirement: 55-year affordability (raised from 30 years in 2023) for rental and for-sale units, renewed for 55 years on each resale; resale price capped at purchase price grown by AMI; City first right of refusal on affordable ownership units.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at first approval with an Affordable Housing Plan; Affordable Housing Agreement before final map or building permit. Housing Element Program 8 scheduled a 2024 review of the inclusionary and commercial linkage fee structure; the Council heard a FY 2026-27 Master Fee Schedule and nexus study update in March 2026, so confirm the current per square foot rate with Planning Services.)
- Layering notes: San Ramon's 15% rental requirement with half the units at very low income is the deepest in the county among the priority cities and, combined with Bishop Ranch's build-out, produces receiver-site deals: the Canopy (BR 8) Affordable Site Development Agreement introduced January 13, 2026 (Ordinance 536, adopted January 27, 2026) has Sunset Development dedicating a rough-graded site with impact fees paid to Eden Housing for 161 affordable units that absorb the inclusionary obligations of 255 Canopy single-family homes (raised from 15% to 22.5%) and the CityWalk apartments, plus $3,000 per market-rate unit (about $765,000) paid into the Affordable Housing Fund. Dougherty Valley affordable units (Highlands Point, Muirlands, Seville, Valencia, Cornerstone at Gale Ranch and others, about 1,886 affordable units citywide) are governed by Contra Costa County affordability agreements under the Dougherty Valley Settlement Agreement and the County's Chapter 822-4, not this ordinance, and several 20-year moderate-income agreements expire in 2026. Ordinance text read at source_url; the Canopy staff report was read on the City's IQM2 agenda host (https://sanramonca.iqm2.com/Citizens/Detail_LegiFile.aspx?ID=4882).

### City of Santa Ana

**Affordable Housing Development RFP No. 26-004A (Inclusionary Housing Fund, HOME, HOME-ARP and Housing Successor Agency loans)**
- Agency: City of Santa Ana Community Development Agency, Housing Division, 20 Civic Center Plaza M-26, (714) 667-2250; bid contact Jacques Lam, JLam@santa-ana.org; solicitation on PlanetBids portal 20137
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Open RFP issued May 1, 2026 with $17,507,926 available: Inclusionary Housing Funds $2,628,194, HOME $11,533,196, HOME-ARP $715,622 (permanent supportive housing only), Housing Successor Agency Funds $2,630,914, plus Housing Authority project-based vouchers and Housing Successor land. Available funds are republished each quarter in the Housing Division Quarterly Report and added to the RFP by addendum. Recent City awards: Crossroads at Washington $4,600,000 plus 15 PBVs (86 units), WISEPlace $5,200,000 plus 25 PBVs (48 units), Estrella Springs $1,600,000 plus 89 PBVs (89 units), Wellington $920,000 (9 ownership units, approved July 1, 2025), Richard Lehn Intergenerational Housing $2,021,319 HHAP plus 8 PBVs (11 units).
- AMI requirement: At least 55-year covenants; Inclusionary and Housing Successor funds serve moderate (120% AMI), low, very low and extremely low income households and may fund mixed-income and mixed-use projects; HOME units at High and Low HOME rents with 20% of HOME-assisted units at 50% AMI in projects of five or more HOME units; HOME-ARP units are permanent supportive housing only. Priority points for substantial rehabilitation and adaptive reuse (motel and office conversions), homeownership, and by-right or shovel-ready projects.
- Cycle: rolling (quarterly deadlines under a one-year open RFP) (next: Quarterly proposal deadlines: January 11, 2027 and May 3, 2027 at 4:00 p.m. (July 1 and October 1, 2026 rounds have passed); question deadlines November 30, 2026 and April 5, 2027. The City's stated objective is to issue one affordable housing RFP per year and finance at least one multifamily project per year.)
- Layering notes: Santa Ana is the deepest city pool in Orange County: about $17,500,000 in one RFP, mostly HOME, with loans at 3% simple interest, 55-year term, repaid from 50% of residual receipts, TCAC developer fee limits and a Review Panel scoring process under the 2020 Affordable Housing Funds Policies and Procedures (opened). City-funded projects must comply with the Community Workforce Agreement (30% of craft hours from Santa Ana and Orange County ZIP codes, union hiring halls) and state prevailing wage; Davis-Bacon applies to HOME projects of 12 or more assisted units. Stack with County 2026 Supportive Housing NOFA loans and OCHA or SAHA PBVs, OCHFT gap loans (WISEPlace took $2,500,000 OCHFT MHSA plus $1,500,000 County ARPA) and 4% or 9% credits. The County NOFA pays $95,000 to $105,000 per unit inside Santa Ana, so the City loan is normally the larger local layer. RFP PDF, RFP page, policies PDF and FY 2025-26 Q4 quarterly report opened on santa-ana.gov and its Google Cloud document store.

**Affordable Housing Opportunity and Creation Ordinance (Municipal Code Chapter 41, Article XVIII.I, Secs. 41-1900 to 41-1909; Ordinance NS-3019) and in-lieu fee to the Inclusionary Housing Fund**
- Agency: City of Santa Ana Planning and Building Agency (inclusionary housing plans) and Community Development Agency Housing Division (Inclusionary Housing Fund)
- Type: other
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. Applies to projects of five or more units (lowered from 20 by NS-3019, adopted April 19, 2022) that receive a discretionary density or land use increase. Rental projects: 15% low income, or 10% very low, or 5% extremely low, or a 10% mix (5% low, 3% very low, 2% extremely low). For-sale projects: 5% moderate income. In-lieu fee per habitable square foot on a tiered schedule of $6.00, $9.00, $12.00 and $15.00 by project size, with the $15.00 rate for 20 or more units reducible to $10.00 or $5.00 when the developer commits to local hire (30% of hours) and skilled and trained workforce percentages. The earlier NS-2994 amendment had cut the fee from $15 to $5 per square foot before the 2022 rewrite. Inclusionary Housing Fund receipts since inception: $31,147,483 (FY 2009-2020 $10,800,251; FY 20/21 $3,709,875; FY 21/22 $6,933,320; FY 22/23 $0; FY 23/24 $834,000; FY 24/25 $0; FY 25/26 $1,685,995 from the 408-unit Lowe Enterprises project at 2828 N. Main St.). Fund expenditures to date $20,558,250 for 224 units plus The Link interim shelter ($7,893,866); commitments $1,357,021. Only 35 on-site inclusionary units (25 ownership, 10 rental) have been built since 2011, so the ordinance functions mainly as a fee.
- AMI requirement: On-site units restricted 55 years; fund may be spent on moderate, low, very low and extremely low income rental and ownership housing, shelter and down payment assistance. Sec. 41-1904.1 incentives for on-site production: up to 25% setback reduction, up to 20 feet of added height, and a local density bonus of 1.5% for each 1% of for-sale units above 5% moderate income, up to 35%.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at entitlement; fee due before building permit. Fee schedule may be changed only by a five-vote Council supermajority (Sec. 41-1904(c)). The Housing Element programs commit the City to periodic review of the threshold and fee.)
- Layering notes: This fee stream feeds the Inclusionary Housing Fund that is offered through the City's annual Affordable Housing Development RFP (record above), which is the only Orange County city in-lieu fund with a regular competitive outlet. Orange County has no county inclusionary ordinance, so this is a city-only requirement. Market-rate developers often use the ordinance's local density bonus with the state bonus; the Housing Element notes the 2022 rewrite was meant to recover fee revenue lost after NS-2994 cut the rate to $5. Ordinance page, NS-3019 PDF and the zoneomics code mirror for Article XVIII.I opened; fund figures from the FY 2025-26 Q4 Housing Division Quarterly Report (opened).
- Source: https://santa-ana.gov/2021-affordable-housing-opportunity-and-creation-ordinance/
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Density Bonus for Affordable Housing (Municipal Code Chapter 41, Article XVI.I, Secs. 41-1600 to 41-1607) and Density Bonus Agreements**
- Agency: City of Santa Ana Planning and Building Agency, Planning Division, (714) 667-2700
- Type: density bonus
- Typical award: Requirement and entitlement, not a subsidy. The local article grants a 25% density bonus plus one additional development incentive under a recorded Density Bonus Agreement, with waivers or modifications of development standards decided under Sec. 41-1607; state law (Government Code 65915) now governs bonus amounts up to 50% or more, up to five incentives or concessions and unlimited waivers, and the City applies the state schedule. The FY 2025-26 Q4 Housing Division report lists the Density Bonus Agreements executed to date, including 415 and 547 rental units restricted under two agreements and smaller sets of 92, 19, 11 and 2 very low income units.
- AMI requirement: State law thresholds: 5% very low, 10% low, 10% moderate for-sale, or 100% affordable; local code covenants of 30 years when an additional incentive is granted (state law requires 55 years for rental); a monitoring fee set by resolution applies.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at project application; agreements recorded before building permit.)
- Layering notes: Santa Ana projects routinely combine the state density bonus with the AHOCO local bonus and the Transit Zoning Code (SD-84) and Metro East overlays; the Housing Element credits the City with 5,130 permits from 2021 to 2024, 152% of its very low, low and moderate RHNA progress through 2025. No fee waiver or impact fee deferral ordinance for affordable housing was found; the County NOFA treats city fee waivers as match but Santa Ana offers none. Density bonus alone does not trigger prevailing wage. Code text read on the zoneomics mirror; the Q4 quarterly report lists agreements.

**HOME Investment Partnerships, CDBG and ESG entitlement (FY 2025-2029 Consolidated Plan)**
- Agency: City of Santa Ana Community Development Agency, Housing Division (HOME Participating Jurisdiction since 1994)
- Type: grant
- Typical award: Five-year Consolidated Plan FY 2025-2029 anticipates $41,700,000: CDBG $30,123,118, HOME $9,093,495, ESG $2,504,870. HOME development funds are deployed as loans through the Affordable Housing Development RFP ($11,533,196 of HOME and $715,622 of HOME-ARP available in RFP 26-004A), with 15% of each annual HOME allocation reserved for certified CHDOs. CDBG funds public services, infrastructure, the Residential Rehabilitation Program (grants up to $25,000, closed in Q4 FY 2025-26 when funds ran out) and shelter; HOME also funds the My First Home mortgage assistance program.

Davis-Bacon applies at 12 or more HOME-assisted units; HOME brings NEPA, Section 3 and a HUD subsidy layering review. HOME-ARP is limited to permanent supportive housing. Santa Ana is outside the County Urban County program, so County HOME is not available inside the city. ### City of Santa Rosa

**Permanent Local Housing Allocation (PLHA), City of Santa Rosa formula allocation and 2024-2028 PLHA Plan**
- Agency: City of Santa Rosa Housing and Community Services Department; loans awarded by the Housing Authority through its NOFA
- Type: loan
- Typical award: Five-year 2024-2028 formula allocation of up to $3,046,056 ($487,369 for 2024 and $522,044 for 2025 applied for after an October 13, 2026 public hearing); up to 5% ($152,303) for administration. The prior 2019-2023 allocation of $4,012,612 was committed to four projects totaling 196 units. Funds are loaned at 3% simple interest, deferred, repaid from surplus cash, secured by deed of trust and regulatory agreement.

Petaluma also receives its own PLHA (see Petaluma record). Because PLHA, CDBG, PIP, HOME and local Housing Trust money all flow through the same NOFA, one application reaches all City sources. **Santa Rosa Affordable Housing Capital Facilities Fee Pilot Program (Resolution RES-2024-175) and 50% permit fee reduction for 100% deed-restricted projects**
- Agency: City of Santa Rosa Planning and Economic Development Department with Housing and Community Services (deed restrictions through the Housing Authority)
- Type: fee waiver
- Typical award: Capital Facilities Fee (Chapter 21-04) set at $0 for new units deed-restricted through the Housing Authority at very low (0-50% AMI, including acutely and extremely low), low (50-80% AMI) and moderate (80-120% AMI) income levels, for building permits issued during the three-year pilot (adopted late 2024, runs until about late 2027 or adoption of a new CFF nexus study, whichever is first). The City's 2026 Prohousing renewal application also cites a 50 percent reduction in permit fees for projects in which 100 percent of units are deed-restricted affordable, and streamlined design review. The CFF for a multifamily unit is several thousand dollars, so the waiver is worth roughly $100,000 to $500,000 on a typical project (confirm with the current fee schedule).
- AMI requirement: Units must be deed-restricted through the Housing Authority at the AMI categories above. Units receiving locally sourced financial assistance from the City or Housing Authority loan programs are NOT eligible for the CFF waiver.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies to building permits for vertical construction issued during the pilot period (three years from the late 2024 effective date of RES-2024-175, roughly through fall 2027, unless a new nexus study ends it sooner). Permit fee reduction has no stated sunset.)
- Layering notes: Key conflict: a project cannot take both the CFF waiver and a Santa Rosa Housing Trust NOFA loan, so model both paths; for a 100% affordable LIHTC deal the NOFA loan is usually larger than the CFF waiver, but the waiver has no competition and no application cycle. The waiver stacks with the Chapter 21-01 deferral of other impact fees, state density bonus and the County welfare exemption (county record). The County's 2025-2026 traffic and parks fee waiver (county record) applies only in unincorporated Sonoma County. Read from the resolution text included in the City's draft 2026 Prohousing Designation renewal application (Legistar matter 26-0547, Council hearing August 4, 2026); the City's designation expires January 1, 2027 and renewal is pending with HCD.

**Santa Rosa Density Bonus and Other Developer Incentives, Zoning Code Chapter 20-31 (state density bonus plus local Supplemental Density Bonus up to 100%)**
- Agency: City of Santa Rosa Planning and Economic Development Department; Density Bonus Housing Agreements through the Housing Authority
- Type: density bonus
- Typical award: Regulatory, not cash. State density bonus up to 50% with incentives and concessions; 100% affordable rental projects (very low and low income, up to 20% moderate) get a 100% density bonus. Local enhancements: (1) an Additional Density Bonus of up to 100% above maximum density for projects that reach the 50% base bonus and add very low income units (5% additional VLI units earns 20%, up to 10% VLI earns 38.75%) or moderate income units; (2) a Supplemental Density Bonus through a Minor Conditional Use Permit using Eligibility Points, at least 60% earned by on-site affordable units and up to 40% by community benefits (public open space, park or capital facilities fee contributions, landmark rehabilitation, family-sized affordable units), with three total incentives or concessions; (3) incentives for specialized housing (10% of units for special needs at very low income rents, 55 years) and child care facilities.
- AMI requirement: Affordable units restricted 55 years under a recorded Density Bonus Housing Agreement; inclusionary units may count toward both Chapter 21-02 and the density bonus.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Density bonus application filed with the first entitlement application and processed concurrently; Supplemental Density Bonus requires a Minor CUP. Chapter last amended by Ordinance 2023-006 (June 6, 2023); further Title 20 amendments to implement the 2023-2031 Housing Element were introduced December 2025 (PLN25-0397).)
- Layering notes: Santa Rosa's supplemental bonus goes beyond state law and beyond the County's Chapter 26 density bonus program (county record), which is useful on infill sites near the two SMART stations and Downtown where the Downtown Station Area Specific Plan already allows high densities. A single affordability agreement can cover inclusionary and density bonus units. Pairing a 100% density bonus with the CFF pilot waiver and the Housing Trust NOFA is the standard local stack. Read from the ecode360 mirror of the Santa Rosa City Code.

- Agency: Housing Authority of the City of Santa Rosa, Housing and Community Services Department (Santa Rosa Housing Trust)
- Type: loan
- Typical award: FY 2026-27 NOFA (issued May 1, 2026, due June 5, 2026): about $3.6 million, made up of about $1,399,000 local Housing Trust funds, $1,056,071 CDBG and $1,187,500 state Prohousing Incentive Program (PIP) funds; two applications received for $4 million and 93 units; August 24, 2026 awards: $2,000,000 to Ponderosa Village Phase II (CRDC and Danco, 30 units, 250 Roseland Ave) and $1,642,571 to Caritas Homes Phase II (360 Seventh St). FY 2025-26 NOFA: about $3.5 million (about $2,210,500 local, $1,082,310 CDBG); awards Sept 2025: $489,228 Zane-Wolff Veterans Village rehab, $1,238,310 Apple Valley Scattered Sites rehab, $2,000,000 Ridley Family Apartments (50 units). FY 2024-25: about $3.1 million for 170 units. The City's own PLHA 2024-2028 allocation (separate record) and the $1.25 million PIP grant (accepted April 7, 2026, must be spent by June 30, 2028) are folded into this NOFA, so a single application reaches all City sources; applicants cannot pick the source. **Santa Rosa Inclusionary Housing Ordinance, City Code Chapter 21-02 (Housing Allocation Plan): on-site allocated units, housing impact fee and commercial linkage fee**
- Agency: City of Santa Rosa Planning and Economic Development Department (compliance) and Housing Authority (affordability agreements and fee proceeds)
- Type: other
- Typical award: Requirement, not a subsidy. For-rent projects: 8% of units for low income or 5% for very low income households; for-sale: 10% moderate income; Downtown multifamily: 4% low or 3% very low (rental) and 5% moderate (for-sale). Projects of six or fewer units pay the housing impact fee. Any project may instead pay the housing impact fee set by Council resolution, indexed to CPI each July (rate not opened this pass; the fee is paid before final inspection for rentals). Commercial linkage fee applies to new commercial development, due at building permit. Collections in 2025: $1,436,870 ($1,257,641 housing impact fees and $179,229 commercial linkage fees), down from $1.52 million in 2024. In 2025, permits were issued for 23 on-site allocated units (20 very low, 2 low, 1 moderate) out of 661 qualifying units.
- AMI requirement: Allocated units restricted 55 years by recorded affordability agreement with the Housing Authority; deed-restricted affordable projects (units restricted 55 years under agreement with the City), homeless shelters, SROs and ADUs are exempt. Fee revenue must fund housing within City limits for lower and moderate income households with 55-year agreements; Downtown fees are reserved two years for Downtown projects.
- Cycle: rolling (next: Applies at entitlement; fee rate in effect at payment. Council reviewed the 2025 General Plan and Inclusionary Housing Annual Review on March 17, 2026; the next annual review is expected in March 2027. HAP last substantively amended by Ordinance 2019-015 (Ordinance 3998 of October 22, 2019).)
- Layering notes: Fee proceeds feed the Santa Rosa Housing Trust NOFA (record above), so market-rate pipeline volume drives local loan capacity. Developers providing on-site units get one incentive or concession under Chapter 20-31 and may count the same units toward a state density bonus (bonus units are excluded from the base when computing the inclusionary share). Alternatives (off-site units in the same quadrant, land dedication, conversion of market-rate units, preservation of at-risk units, inclusionary credits usable for 10 years) require Director approval; off-site units cannot receive City or Housing Authority subsidy. The County's separate Affordable Housing Program fee applies only in unincorporated areas. Read on the ecode360 mirror of the Santa Rosa City Code because qcode.us and srcity.org block scripts; collection data from the 2025 Annual Review (Legistar matter 26-0150).
- Source: https://ecode360.com/42997624
- Confidence: verified (researched 2026-11-08)

**Santa Rosa development fee deferral for affordable housing units, City Code Chapter 21-01 (Section 21-01.020)**
- Agency: City of Santa Rosa Planning and Economic Development Department; agreements approved by City Council
- Type: fee waiver
- Typical award: Deferral, not a waiver: Government Code 66000(b) development impact fees on affordable units under contract with the City may be deferred up to two years from the date otherwise due, secured by a deed of trust, with the balance (at the rate in effect when originally due) payable on sale, transfer or placement of permanent financing. Separately, all City development impact fees are due at final inspection rather than permit issuance (Section 21-01.030), which is itself a cash-flow benefit, and water and sewer demand fees may use a Board of Public Utilities payment plan.

The County's Multi-Family Development Fee Deferral Program (county record) applies only to unincorporated projects. Deferral agreements are not assignable without City Attorney consent, which matters when a LIHTC partnership takes title after entitlement. Read from the ecode360 mirror; the Housing Element implementation ordinance introduced December 2025 (PLN25-0397) amended Titles 20 and 21 but the redline was not reviewed for changes to this chapter.

### City of Sonoma

The City's housing strategies page still states the City does not require housing impact fees for projects below five units or for commercial projects without housing, so adoption of the residential fee is unconfirmed.
